clue.text: Shut up about Charlie's inclination

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: shut up means confined, pent (as in pent-up)
Charlie Chan is the fictional Chinese-American detective of novels and films, so Charlie gives his surname

explanation.surface: Someone's fondness for keeping quiet on the subject of Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CHAN inside PENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong liking or leaning towards something is a synonym for an inclination.

clue.text: Noble that is — Roundhead before that

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
the head of the word Round is its first letter

explanation.surface: A nobleman, that is to say a parliamentarian of the English Civil War, came first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundhead' suggests a parliamentarian of the English Civil War but gives just the first letter of 'Round'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happened sooner, at a previous time, happened before that.

clue.text: Touchstone in the theatre

definitions.meaning: a standard by which other things are judged
a well-known playhouse in London's Piccadilly Circus

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a standard for judging things, and it is also the name of a famous London theatre.

clue.text: Nervous first-nighter ?

parts.note: suggests an anxious audience member, but the person most anxious at a play's opening night is its writer

explanation.surface: Someone jittery attending a premiere.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright is the most anxious person at a premiere, waiting for the verdict on their work.

clue.text: A classic turning point in racing

definitions.text: A classic turning point in racing

parts.words: A classic turning point in racing
parts.note: reads as a decisive moment in sport, but means the famous bend on a course hosting one of the five Classic flat races

explanation.surface: A celebrated moment that changed the course of horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tattenham Corner is the sharp bend on Epsom Downs, home of the Derby, one of Britain's five Classic horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the bend before the home straight at Epsom racecourse, where the Derby, a Classic race, is run.

clue.text: Drove badly and skidded outside the church

indicators.note: outside means the first piece sits around the second, here wrapping the church

parts.note: to skid is to slide, past tense slid
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A motorist's poor driving ended in a skid just beyond the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove' looks like motoring but is golf: a slice is a bad drive curving away. 'outside' puts SLID around CE.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a sliced shot is a drive struck badly so the ball curves off to one side.

clue.text: Easy job to get about in

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to secure something is to get or obtain it

explanation.surface: An undemanding post that someone wants to obtain a way into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IN inside SECURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid position needing little or no work.

clue.text: It throws light on obscure secrets.

indicators.note: to obscure is to blur or confuse, so the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that reveals hidden secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' looks like an adjective but is a verb telling you to scramble SECRETS; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset is an iron basket of burning fuel used as a torch or beacon.

clue.text: Talk of a career in the underworld?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
a course is a career or path through life

explanation.surface: A discussion about a job in organised crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the underworld' suggests gangsters but means Dis, the classical underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal talk or speech on a subject.

clue.text: One who is pro hanging ?

parts.note: reads like a supporter of capital punishment, but a painter is in favour of having works hung in a gallery

explanation.surface: A person who favours the death penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR gives 'banging'; the clue needs 'hanging'. A painter wants pictures hung in exhibitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters want their pictures hung on gallery walls, so a painter is all for a hanging.

clue.text: Lets one's constitution become flat

indicators.note: constitution means make-up or composition, so these letters are made up afresh

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone allows their health to become dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitution' as the make-up of a thing tells you to rebuild LETSONES into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice without any tone or expression sounds flat, so the two words are synonyms here.

clue.text: Old woman consumes ice, given by the guide

indicators.note: consumes means takes in, so the first piece swallows the second

parts.note: a crone is an old woman

explanation.surface: An elderly woman eats an ice cream handed to her by a tour guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' puts ICE inside CRONE; 'given by the' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicerone is a guide who shows sightseers around, named after the eloquent Roman orator.

clue.text: Company holds a ship with one Shakespearian lieutenant

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the first piece wraps round the others

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A firm owns a vessel captained by a lieutenant from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts A, SS and I inside CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassio is Othello's lieutenant in Shakespeare's tragedy, whom Iago frames.

clue.text: Nail round one trimming

indicators.note: round means going around, so the nail encloses the numeral

parts.note: a brad is a thin flat nail
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Fixing a nail around a single decorative edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts I inside BRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Braid is a woven band used as decorative trimming on clothes and uniforms.

clue.text: Coverlet layers BC ?

parts.note: beds are layers, as of rock
before Christ is the period before AD, i.e. pre-AD

explanation.surface: A blanket with strata dating from antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: BC, before Christ, is read as PRE-AD, the time before Anno Domini.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is the decorative top cover laid over a bed.

clue.text: " These few precepts… Look thou — " (Hamlet)

parts.note: Polonius tells Laertes: 'And these few precepts in thy memory / Look thou' and a verb meaning engrave or inscribe, which fills the gap

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Polonius tells his son to inscribe his advice in his memory.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's usage the verb meant to inscribe or engrave, as letters are written.

clue.text: Bird is an angry old battle axe

parts.note: cross means angry
a bill was an old weapon, a long-handled hooked blade

explanation.surface: A bird is a furious old harridan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battle axe' suggests a fierce old woman, but it is the bill, a medieval weapon; 'is an' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbill is a finch whose bill tips cross over, used to prise seeds from cones.

clue.text: -, and hoping to get seat no doubt

definitions.text: -, and hoping to get seat no doubt

parts.words: -, and hoping to get seat no doubt
parts.note: the gap is filled by a word for being upright, as a passenger is on a crowded train, also a candidate's act of running for a seat

explanation.surface: A passenger upright and wanting somewhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: A parliamentary candidate stands for election, hoping to win a seat; a bus passenger stands and hopes to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upright on one's feet, or contesting an election, both fit someone hoping for a seat.

clue.text: Period of activity for convicts?

parts.note: reads as a spell of busy work, but the phrase is the idiom for serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Asking when prisoners are kept busy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase is a time of doing things; idiomatically it is serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving a prison sentence is idiomatically described this way, and the literal sense is being active over a stretch.

clue.text: Tick-it's urgent

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a moment; as an adjective it means immediate or pressing.

clue.text: A cut above the ordinary saloon ?

definitions.text: A cut above the ordinary saloon ?

parts.words: A cut above the ordinary saloon ?
parts.note: a two-door sports-style car is classier than a standard saloon car, and its French name literally means cut

explanation.surface: A car that is superior to the everyday family model.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is the British word for a sedan car. The French word for this car body is the past participle of couper, to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupé is a two-door car with a shortened, sloping roof; in French the word means cut.

clue.text: Like a Repton pater on Peon art, part one, near top

definitions.text: Like a Repton pater on Peon art, part one, near top

parts.words: Like a Repton pater on Peon art, part one, near top
parts.note: every phrase after 'Like a' uses the same seven letters in a different order, showing a word that takes many shapes

explanation.surface: A fatherly figure from a school discussing peasant art.
explanation.walkthrough: Repton, pater on, Peon art, part one and near top are all rearrangements of the same letters, a set of shape-changers; Repton is an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Protean means changing form readily, like the sea-god Proteus, just as these letters keep rearranging.

clue.text: A word of approval about copper's penetration

indicators.note: about means around, so the word of approval goes around the symbol

parts.note: amen is said to express agreement or approval
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Praise for a policeman's insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal, Cu. 'about' puts CU inside AMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight or shrewdness, the ability to see deep into things.

clue.text: Gone on literary letters

parts.note: gone by means past

explanation.surface: A collection of famous correspondence has moved on.
explanation.walkthrough: The Paston Letters are a famous fifteenth-century collection of a Norfolk family's correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paston Letters, written by a Norfolk gentry family in the 1400s, are a celebrated literary source on medieval English life.

clue.text: Provoke, with reason

definitions.meaning: to cause or bring about, used as a verb
a ground or cause, as in 'no cause for alarm'

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to bring about or cause; as a noun it means a cause or ground for something.

clue.text: Right one dealing with an exorbitant tax

parts.note: exact means correct or right
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A correct person handling an outrageously high levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like a direction or entitlement but gives EXACT, meaning precise.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is an excessive demand for payment, especially an extortionate levy.

clue.text: Many were sick of being posted

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, used for many
ailed means were ill

explanation.surface: Lots of people were fed up with being sent away somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick of' looks like fed up with, but 'were sick' gives AILED and 'of being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter that has been posted has been sent by mail.

clue.text: Becoming old hat

parts.note: describes something going out of fashion, sounding like an ageing piece of headwear

explanation.surface: A hat getting old.
explanation.definitionFit: A style that is dating is starting to look out of fashion, which is what old hat means.

clue.text: Bad fish, still causing pain

parts.note: rank means foul or rotten
a ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Rotten fish that still hurts after eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like 'nonetheless' but belongs to the definition: continuing to cause pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance that keeps festering and hurting is said to be rankling.
